items.heading: Explains the ten Sefirot of Yosher (Straightness), their emergence and cascading, and what is included in them. It contains seven topics: — The order of the emergence of the ten Sefirot of Yosher
items.html: Now we shall explain the second aspect that is in the ten Sefirot, namely, the aspect of the light of Yosher (Straightness), like the illustration of three lines, in the form of the Upper Man. Now, along the path of the aforementioned line, which expands from above downward, and from which the circles expand, that line too expands in straightness from above downward, from the top 1of the roof of the highest of all the circles, down to below the bottom of the conclusion of all the circles literally, from above downward, comprised of ten Sefirot, by the secret of 2the image of a straight man, 3of erect stature, 4comprised of two hundred and forty-eight organs, formed in the shape of three lines — right, left, and middle — comprised of ten Sefirot in general, and each and every Sefira of them is detailed into ten Sefirot, without end.

items.heading: The five parts of the soul in the lower man: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida
items.html: Now, 5the lower man has five aspects of lights, which are: 6Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, and Yechida. And they are 7five levels, one above the other, and this is the secret of the five instances of “Bless the Lord, O my soul” etc., as mentioned in tractate Berachot (page 10a), which correspond to the five aspects that the soul has.

items.heading: Both in the circles and in Yosher there is surrounding light and inner light, an external vessel and an internal vessel
items.html: Now, the aspect of the ten Sefirot of all the circles contains all the aforementioned aspects, which are: 8lights and vessels, 9and the light divides into inner light and surrounding light, 10and the vessel divides into externality and internality. Likewise, the aspect of the ten Sefirot of Yosher in the form of a man contains all these very same aspects as well.

items.heading: The light of the circles is the light of Nefesh, and the light of Yosher is the light of Ruach. First the circles were emanated, and afterward Yosher
items.html: However, the difference between the circles and Yosher is that 11the ten Sefirot of the circles are the aspect of the light called Nefesh, and they contain inner light and surrounding light, internal and external: they have the aspect of ten Sefirot of vessels, and in each vessel of them there is internality and externality, and there are also ten Sefirot of lights, and each light contains inner light and surrounding light within it. But the ten Sefirot of Yosher are the aspect of the light called 12Ruach, which is a level higher than the level of Nefesh, as is known; they too are comprised of inner light and surrounding light, and they too have ten Sefirot of vessels, and in each vessel of them there is internality and externality. And it is self-evident that the aspect of Nefesh was emanated first, and afterward Ruach was emanated.

items.heading: Arich Anpin of the circles illuminates Abba and Ima of the circles, by way of windows from its three lines — right, left, and middle. And from them the light is extended to all the circles, in a manner that all the details that exist in Yosher exist likewise in the circles
items.html: *Also, in the ten Sefirot being in the aspect of 13circles, one within the other, there are 14all the aspects of the reception of the flow that exist in the ten Sefirot of the line of Yosher, and this is because in the circle of Keter, called 15Arich Anpin after the correction, there is 16one perforation and a window 17on the right side of the circle, and from there 18the light of Arich descends to the circle of Abba, and illuminates it. There is also a second window, on the left of the circle of Arich, and the light goes out to the left side of the circle of Abba, within which, 19it too is perforated and a window is made in it, and from there the light is extended to the circle of Ima, which is within the circle of Abba, and illuminates it. Thus it is found that the light passing through the left side of the circle of Abba is not for Abba himself, and does not 20pass there except merely as a passage, but the main illumination is for Ima. It is thus found that Arich Anpin illuminates Abba and Ima together, exactly as is the case with their aspect in Yosher. And although they are circles one within the other, they have 21straight lines — right, left, and middle — by way of these windows that are in them. And from there the light is extended in the ten Sefirot of the circles, by way of literally straight lines, in all the very details that are in the ten Sefirot of the straight line of Ruach, literally.

items.heading: Adam Kadmon extends from Ein Sof to the end of Atzilut, and all the worlds are included in it. And we have no permission to engage with it
items.html: *Now, 400this Adam Kadmon 1passes through from one end to the other, from the uppermost end to the lowermost end, throughout the aforementioned space of Atzilut. And in this Man all the worlds are included, as will be explained, God willing, but 2as for the internal aspect and the very self of this Man, we have no permission to speak of it or to engage with it at all.

items.heading: First the circles emerged, and afterward Yosher. We deal not with the circles but with Yosher alone
items.html: However, 3at first the ten Sefirot emerged by way of circles, one within the other, and afterward, within the circles, there extended by way of Yosher, like the form of a single man, 4along the length of all the aforementioned circles, 5and we do not deal at all with the aspect of circles, but only with the aspect of Yosher alone.
